data.title: Ed Sheeran hit by viral false claims after Macklemore controversy

Vedika Bahl fact-checks in Truth or Fake.

data.title: The truth about Sean Combs: ‘No is not a stopping point for him’
data.description: Cheyenne Roundtree, an investigative reporter at Rolling Stone, was as shocked as anyone when allegations of rape and sexual abuse were made against the music mogul. Then she began digging into his past life. In her first interview, she paints a horrifying picture of lost police reports, repeat behaviours, rumours and run-ins For Cheyenne Roundtree, an investigative reporter at Rolling Stone, the civil lawsuit that dropped on Sean “Diddy” Combs in November 2023 seemed to come from nowhere. Filed by his ex-partner, the singer Cassie Ventura, it alleged that Combs had beaten and raped her, plied her with drugs and forced her into sexual encounters with male sex workers throughout their decade-long relationship. Roundtree, along with much of the world’s media, was shocked. “I’d grown up in the era of Diddy and Cassie and viewed them as this power couple,” she says. “Her hit Me & U was my song. Diddy was this mogul – I knew him for the music – and she was this style inspiration, this beautiful, talented woman living an amazing life.” Continue reading...

data.title: Youth review – Sharon Horgan is back … and she’s better than ever
data.description: This brutal, hilarious new show about life as a fiftysomething is full of all the heart and humour of human life. At points it’s mesmerisingly perfect There’s a moment in Sharon Horgan’s new show, Youth, when – as protagonist Alex (Horgan) is seeing her son off to university – she inadvertently begins to run after the car that’s taking him away. And then she catches herself, and slows. And then she starts up again. It was such a tender, vicious glimpse into the future that I found myself sobbing into the sofa and cursing her name. All of which is to say: Sharon Horgan is back and she’s better than ever. Youth is the representation every woman who has ever slapped on an oestrogen patch after a divorce, looked around and thought “What the hell now?” has been waiting for. Horgan herself has described it in interviews as forming the third part of a loose trilogy that began with Pulling. Co-written with Dennis Kelly, Pulling was about three thirtysomething antitheses to Bridget Jones, whose dark chaos apparently scared the BBC so much they unexpectedly cancelled it just as it was truly getting into its stride. That was followed by Catastrophe, written by and starring Horgan, with Rob Delaney, as a couple who have a fling, find that she’s pregnant and end up making a brutal, hilarious go of things. Youth is on HBO Max Continue reading...

data.title: A tale of two trap houses: being cuckooed ruined my friend’s life – but did it then help save him?
data.description: Drug gangs have moved off Britain’s streets and into vulnerable people’s homes. Addicts like my friend are easy targets, but the reality can be more complicated than it seems Duncan is a good friend of mine. He looks like a Dickensian rock’n’roller: tall and skinny, long hair, retro clothes. He’s read the Flashman novels three times. We met in secondary school in west London in the early 1980s. We got drunk, smoked Rothmans and banana skin spliffs and played Dungeons & Dragons. At 14, we got into punk together and spent our teens playing music and seeing live bands. As we moved into our 20s, I trained as a journalist and Duncan, a talented songwriter and guitarist, carried on with music. At the age of 23 he got involved in heroin. He found the lifestyle immediately seductive, his partner at the time, Lucy, told me. He would often befriend his dealers. “I remember more than once waiting in his car as he’d gone up some tower block to score, thinking where on earth is he?” Lucy said. “He’d be hanging out chatting. There were some genuinely fascinating characters with incredible stories to tell.” Continue reading...

data.title: Britain needs cash and everyone knows we should break the pensions triple lock. Where is the courage? | Gaby Hinsliff
data.description: The issue cannot be avoided any longer. Andy Burnham and his chancellor must face the fear of a pensioner backlash, and find a fair solution There is always something oddly unreal about party conference season. In theory, everyone is getting away from Westminster to better reflect on the state of the nation. In practice, the whole circus just briefly relocates to the coast, to live off warm white wine and gossip for three days, before coming back with a streaming cold. But this year, reality seems more elusive than usual. Everyone knows hard choices loom, but everyone is frightened to make them. Every serious party needs billions of pounds to fund their promises, and everyone knows there’s an obvious place to find the money, but nobody wants to be the first to say so. And so a deferential silence shrouds the pension triple lock, whose future will be vigorously debated on the fringes and in private conversation this autumn, but less so on the stage. Gaby Hinsliff is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: The pest I’ll never forget: I awoke to the sound of my bedroom bin rustling
data.description: At first the mice were just a distant pitter-patter. But soon they had an unblinking confidence that they owned the entire house and all the food in it Living in a nine-person house in Vancouver, Canada, far from my UK home, came with plenty of benefits. Cleanliness was not one of them. A dish left behind quickly multiplied and bins overflowed in little more than a day. I’m not saying the endless strew of disposable coffee cups was the cause of our year-long mice infestation, but it no doubt helped. In the winter of 2023, one of my housemates began to hear the sound of creatures rattling around in the ceiling of her basement room. The pitter-patters grew louder and louder; others began to report sightings from across the house. It wasn’t long before I was waking to the sound of my bedroom bin rustling. I had to accept it: we had mice. Continue reading...

data.title: From paleo to intermittent fasting: are any diets actually good for us? - podcast
data.description: As diet trends proliferate on social media, it can be hard to work out which are backed by science and which should be ignored. From paleo to keto, raw food to intermittent fasting, each attracts a tribe of ardent followers. Now Daniel Lieberman, professor of biological sciences at Harvard University, has written a book to try to cut through the noise. In Fed Up, he uses his background as an evolutionary anthropologist to scrutinise the evidence, turning himself into a guinea pig in the process and trying various diets. In this podcast, he tells Ian Sample which one has remained part of his routine Order Fed Up from the Guardian Bookshop Support the Guardian: theguardian.com/sciencepod Continue reading...

data.title: Grief, trauma and solidarity as South African running club mourns member killed in wave of femicides
data.description: A week after Elizabeth ‘Tsontso’ Moselakgomo’s body was found, runners took part in a morning run to honour her name and demand more protection The runners smiled and laughed, congratulating each other on finishing their 5km or 10km Saturday run, their foreheads glistening with sweat in the early morning sun. They helped themselves to water, instant coffee and sugary snacks, provided by waiting volunteers on the lawn outside a gated community of modern apartment blocks, and then stretched out together. But there were sombre moments too, as they mourned one of their own, who had lit up their Saturday runs around Sandton, an upmarket area of Johannesburg. Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo’s body had been found a week earlier, on Saturday 12 September. The 38-year-old went missing three days earlier, after going out for a run alone after work. data.title: The truth about UK prisons and organised crime: ‘They’re your good lads. Respectful. Keep their noses clean’
data.description: In more than two decades in the Prison Service, Pia Sinha gained a reputation as a fixer. Now, as head of the Prison Reform Trust, she’s sounding the alarm about overcrowding and other problems Pia Sinha has led the Prison Reform Trust since 2023. In that time, she has seen a Conservative government finally admit to an overcrowding crisis that had tipped over the edge. (It was in October 2023 that the early release scheme was devised; by May 2024, the Tories had also launched Operation Safeguard , using police cells as temporary housing.) She’s watched a change of government, then a change of prime minister, then Andy Burnham instantly assailed by negative headlines as the consequences of that early release scheme unfolded: prisoners had to actually be released early. “We’re a bit concerned about how [Burnham] has handled it,” she says, in the trust’s scruffy, un-corporate offices in central London, “but that’s in the knowledge that he had a bit of a hospital pass.” To recap on Burnham’s handling: when he came in in July, he paused the scheme for an urgent review; in August he announced a series of exclusions, further crimes for which people couldn’t be released early, including manslaughter and death by dangerous driving. That solved an immediate problem, that the killers of PC Andrew Harper would otherwise have been released, but had the knock-on effect of reducing the numbers expected to be released by about a quarter. The conversation Sinha wants to have is what prison overcrowding looks like, what it does to prisoners and staff – and what it means for society. Continue reading...

data.title: The rise of Big Toothbrush: how did our mouths become such a lucrative market?
data.description: People in the UK are more interested in oral health than ever - and you can now buy prebiotic toothpastes and brushes that cost up to £600. Yet we remain in the midst of a serious dental crisis A December 1969 report from the consumer magazine Which? explored a relatively new gadget that, it predicted, many people would be giving as Christmas presents: the electric toothbrush. For those who hadn’t yet seen one, the magazine described it as “not that much different in principle from an ordinary brush – you have a stick with a brush on the end. The difference is that an electric one moves the brush head for you”. Progress indeed. Nearly six decades on, electric toothbrushes can do a lot more than merely jiggle, offering multiple speeds and movement sensors for real-time tracking of where you’ve brushed – some even promise gum-massage or tongue-cleaning modes. Prices range from about £25 for a basic Oral B model to £599.99 for a Philips Sonicare model that gives “smart coverage feedback”. The latest super-toothbrush – a mere £419.99 – features a camera and a built-in water jet to clean between teeth, using AI to identify gaps. Created by Dyson, it’s still, essentially, a stick with a brush on the end (although there is another toothbrush on the market that’s shaped like a mouthguard, with individual brushes, that claims to clean your teeth in 20 seconds). Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s bordering on exploitation’: how pseudoscience is duping football
data.description: Cryotherapy chambers and other practices have little evidence behind them, says top performance director Dr Claire-Marie Roberts was working at Coventry City when she received a call from someone asking whether she knew how much oxygen was in the atmosphere. As the performance director, responsible for optimising players’ potential, she was accustomed to being pitched the latest gimmick promising miraculous gains. At times, she could receive up to 50 LinkedIn messages a week offering a device, supplement or technology that claimed to produce magical results. “It is only 21%,” the caller told her. That’s GCSE chemistry, she thought. Then came the sales pitch: “So what we’ve done is put oxygen in a can and we think you might want to use it.” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Addiction is not only caused by weak will’: how a talking pigeon got Czechia to face up to its alcohol problem
data.description: Director Pepa Lubojacki’s heartbreaking film chronicles the lives of her brother as he struggles with drink and homelessness – and her own shame in the face of societal prejudice Czech film-maker Pepa Lubojacki originally set out to make a film about pigeons. What fascinated the 39-year-old director was that the grey birds are clearly beautiful and highly intelligent creatures, yet human cruelty towards them is socially acceptable in the way it isn’t towards, say, crows or magpies. “You can spot kids kicking and chasing pigeons while their parents cheerfully look on,” she says. The moral blind spot reminded her of the way that people looked at homeless people like her older brother and her cousins. “The public has learned to avert their eyes,” she says. “My cousin was declined care seven times with open wounds in the hospital, and finally, they had to amputate both of his legs.” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Good music is good music, and most music is not!’ As he hits 90, master minimalist Steve Reich looks back
data.description: At 14, he heard Stravinsky and resolved to be a composer. As Reich approaches his 10th decade, the man revered by the likes of David Bowie reflects on a life that changed the soundtrack of modern living Steve Reich is not yet 90 but the celebrations have already begun, with the world premiere of his new piece for large ensemble, In All Your Ways , at the Edinburgh festival last month and a late-night concert at the BBC Proms . But when I ask this most supremely influential of living composers how he feels about becoming a nonagenarian on 3 October, Reich is coy. “I haven’t quite got there yet,” he says. “I don’t want to dot the i before I even get there. I’ll let you know in due course …” Born in New York in 1936, Reich has spent the last six decades producing music that has changed the soundtrack of modern life in Europe and North America, and inspired superlatives from a wide array of music critics. The New Yorker has called him “the most original musical thinker of our time”. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘To sleep in a sculpture is a wonderful idea’: a hike along Andy Goldsworthy’s epic art trail in Haute-Provence
data.description: A long-distance walking route in the south of France devised by the celebrated land artist offers intrepid hikers an opportunity to immerse themselves in nature and art At 69, I had never hiked with a backpack and I had no idea what land art was. Nonetheless, when my friend Jackie, a nature documentary film-maker, invited me to join her and her friends Wendy and Sasha on a hiking trip to Refuges d’Art in the mountainous countryside of Haute-Provence, I said a resounding “yes”. We would be sleeping alongside sculptures by the renowned land artist Andy Goldsworthy . First, I watch Rivers and Tides , a documentary on Goldsworthy’s work, and discover he has built exquisite ice sculptures and stone cairns in my own country, Canada. His work seems to speak to an older part of the soul. Then, I start walking up hills, gradually adding weights to my backpack until I can comfortably carry 9kg (20lb). Continue reading...

data.title: Europe is under attack from three sides – but the EU and Nato are unfit to defend us | Nathalie Tocci
data.description: Ursula von der Leyen’s outreach to Canada and new security proposals are wise – but she may not be the right messenger Europe’s strategic predicament is ever clearer, and ever darker. The continent is at war, which is being fought militarily in Ukraine, but is escalating rapidly across Europe through hybrid attacks. Germany’s disclosure that it blames Russia for the drone attack at Leipzig airport; a Russian drone strike on a train near the Ukraine-Poland border; an Italian jet shooting down a Russian drone over Lithuania ; flares fired from a Russian warship at a Danish helicopter – all within the space of a couple of weeks – tell a coherent story. Whether because Russia is bogged down and unable to advance in Ukraine, or because it believes the US will not come to Europe’s rescue, Vladimir Putin’s regime is ever more bent on escalating its aggression in Europe. Putin’s calculus is not irrational. Trump never misses a chance to lash out at Europe – the latest example being his threats of further tariffs on the EU if Brussels proceeds to offer Canada “associate membership”. Europeans have grown numb to Trump’s insults and threats, but these threats do underline his deep antipathy, suggesting that if a Russian attack warranted a response, Trump might look the other way. The US certainly can’t be relied on to have Europe’s back. Continue reading...

data.title: Trump still thinks Iranians will ‘rise up’ against the regime. In Tehran I see a different story | Hossein Hamdieh
data.description: If anything, the ongoing war is uniting a divided country against the foreign invaders. Washington seems a long way from grasping this point The US president, Donald Trump, asked recently on one of his Truth Social rants : “When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?” So frenetic and all-over-the-place are Trump’s statements that one does not know which are actual policies and which are simply noise. But if counting on the “Iranian people” to rise up and fight is indeed US policy then, as far as I can tell from within Iran, it is a failed one. And miserably so. At least for now. There is no reliable nationwide polling that can tell us what Iranians think about the war in real time. So this is an observation, not a poll. It comes from conversations I have had with many people. Hossein Hamdieh holds a joint PhD in Geography and Anthropology from Humboldt University of Berlin and King’s College London. data.title: Many Americans live in the UK – but few vote back home. This year, that must change | Kathryn Sikkink
data.description: The rights of overseas voters are protected by US federal law. It’s not hard – but Americans should start planning now The UK hosts the second largest population of voting-age US citizens outside the United States, but Americans living in the UK vote at very low levels in US elections. The US government’s Federal Voting Assistance Program (FVAP) estimated that there were 298,268 voting-age US citizens in the UK in 2022, second only to Canada. But FVAP also estimated that only 3.8% of these US citizens in Britain voted in that year’s midterm elections. Why do hundreds of thousands of eligible US voters in the UK not exercise their right to vote, even though US rules for voting abroad are relatively welcoming compared to many other countries? Continue reading...

data.title: My son has left home – and I feel full of complicated joy | Zoe Williams
data.description: I took him to university this weekend, and it reminded me of the exhilaration of suddenly having your own space, absolutely separate from your mother When kids are small, and their expectations of an event diverge from yours in some important way, you feel terrible about it. You might be taking them to a play, and they thought that meant they’d be allowed to play, but actually it meant they had to sit still while strangers shouted things. You experience their disappointment as much as your own physical pain. Then when they’re “adults”, your expectations diverge again. They thought you’d drop them at university and immediately leave, while you thought you’d unpack, and meet their flatmates, explore the city, and spin round a supermarket, then have a Nando’s, and maybe read a bedtime story, get chatting to the other parents and maybe all do karaoke? Well, then it’s time to manage your own disappointment, and the only thing to be said for that is that it’s way less bad than managing theirs. Continue reading...

Well, then it’s time to manage your own disappointment, and the only thing to be said for that is that it’s way less bad than managing theirs. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Friedrich Merz: Germany’s chancellor must change course to halt the rise of the AfD | Editorial
data.description: A failure to address widespread economic insecurity, and a crisis in living standards, is allowing the far right the harness a growing protest vote After less than a year and a half in office, Germany’s beleaguered chancellor, Friedrich Merz, is already looking like a lame duck leader. Anticipating dire results in two state elections which were held on Sunday, Mr Merz cancelled a planned speech at this week’s United Nations general assembly in order to plot an emergency response. A night of extraordinary humiliation for his conservative Christian Democratic Union party (CDU) must have confounded even his own low expectations. In the eastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the far-right Alternative für Deutschland party (AfD) won its second regional election this month with 38% of the vote. The CDU meanwhile recorded its worst result since the second world war, failing even to meet the 5% threshold for representation in the state parliament. Mr Merz took over the leadership of the CDU promising to see off the threat of the AfD. Instead it has ascended to a menacing and unprecedented position of electoral strength, and enjoys a comfortable lead in national polls. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: The Guardian view on rape courts: ministers know that victims deserve better | Editorial
data.description: New facilities for witnesses who have been sexually assaulted are a step towards halving violence against girls and women The creation of specialist courts to try rape and serious sexual offences in England and Wales is a welcome recognition from the government that the status quo is unacceptable. Victims, the vast majority of whom are women and girls, are being failed by a system that too often appears blind to the obstacles in the way of anyone who wants to see a perpetrator brought to justice. In 2025, rape cases took an average of 424 days after they had reached the crown court . Added to pre‑trial delays, this means thousands of lives being placed on hold for years. Long waits are simply unendurable in many cases; a rape review ordered by Conservative ministers in 2021 found that the proportion of complainants dropping out of cases had risen from 25% to 43% in five years. As well as the harm caused to individuals, there is an obvious impact on public safety when perpetrators go unpunished, and chances to rehabilitate them are missed. data.title: Women’s Champions League: will OL Lyonnes or English trio topple a weakened Barcelona?
data.description: The league phase kicks off this week, with several sides optimistic of unseating the European champions This competition is wide open. “But, wait, you say that every year!” No, honestly, this time it is wide open. The league phase of a new Women’s Champions League campaign begins on Tuesday with genuine elements of unpredictability, intrigue and a competitive feel after Barcelona, the holders, and winners of four titles in six years, underwent significant changes this summer. The Spanish champions, who have reached six European finals in a row, have had four players who started the victory in the final last season leave the club . Ona Batlle joined Arsenal , Salma Paralluelo signed for OL Lyonnes – against whom she scored twice in that 4-0 victory to clinch the title in May – and Alexia Putellas and Mapi León moved to London City Lionesses. They have a very different look and feel to the formidable aura they demonstrated in Oslo. Continue reading...

data.title: Paper trail of protests: José Mourinho plays the hits in Madrid derby defeat | Sid Lowe
data.description: Facing Diego Simeone 13 years on, José Mourinho brought a print-out and paranoia. Some things don’t change. Some people don’t, either There were many questions to emerge from the Madrid derby, which Atlético won 2-1 in front of 70,514 very, very noisy people at the Metropolitano on Sunday afternoon, even if not the one José Mourinho was asking. Like: what year is this? Or: what was Dean Huijsen thinking? Why always Arda? And whatever happened to Vinícius Júnior? How come Koke is still the best? And how long before Giuliano Simeone actually bursts, his atlético insides exploding across the pitch? Above all though, you were left wondering: where did Real Madrid’s manager get a printer from? And how did he get the bloody thing to work? You could still hear the singing outside when Mourinho turned up in the press room, laid down his glasses and sat. In his hand was a piece of paper. Thirteen years after his last derby, on the Santiago Bernabéu night when Madrid lost the Copa del Rey final and a 13-year unbeaten run against their neighbours, Diego Simeone had defeated him again. The stage was new – this stadium didn’t exist then – but his adversary was somehow still the same man, still dressed in black, and the scene was a bit like old times, a classic. Mourinho unfolded the paper and held it up. “We can save ourselves the bother of the press conference,” he said, “because the story is right here.” Continue reading...

data.title: Ghosts of 2023 quelled after Dortmund return to the Bundesliga summit | Andy Brassell
data.description: It is probably a stretch to call BVB title contenders but Niko Kovac’s side maintained their 100% start against Stuttgart Borussia Dortmund would probably rather not think about the last time that they topped the Bundesliga. It was in May 2023, just before all their dreams imploded , with black and yellow Deutscher Meister t-shirts – ‘German champions’ – for sale on the approach to Signal Iduna Park and cold beers at the ready. Now, that is no longer the most recent time Dortmund have led the pack. It’s four games, four wins to start this season and the Niko Kovac workout plan is hitting the spot. Saturday night’s single-goal win at Stuttgart was a game that had the gravitas of a true Topspiel, if not quite the entertainment value of one. Kovac’s fingerprints were all over it. The conversation of whether his view of the game fits with BVB’s swashbuckling image will no doubt continue, but this was a case in point to show just how good Kovac has been for the club, and for the team. Continue reading...

data.title: Granit Xhaka admits to receiving fake Covid vaccination certificate in 2022
data.description: Sunderland captain withdrawn from Switzerland squad He will be questioned by prosecutor’s office in Lucerne Granit Xhaka has been withdrawn from Switzerland’s squad after he admitted receiving a fake Covid vaccination certificate in 2022. The Sunderland and Switzerland captain – who was an Arsenal player at the time – has apologised for this “mistake” and will sit out his country’s forthcoming four Nations League matches. Xhaka is poised to be questioned by the prosecutor’s office in Lucerne next week as it decides whether any criminal proceedings will be initiated regarding the alleged issue of a series of false Covid certificates by a doctor based in the Swiss city during the pandemic. The doctor, who was first investigated in 2023, has denied the allegations. Continue reading...

Cahuzac left Lorient, where he had been Olivier Pantaloni’s assistant, at the end of last season to return to Lens, where he had finished his playing career before working as Franck Haise’s assistant in the 2022–23 campaign. data.title: Meet Barbie Pig: new documentary reveals the wonders of life on the Pacific seabed
data.description: A magical new film captures the secret life of the deep sea in a stretch of the ocean at risk from industrial mining A magical film that explores the wonders of the deep sea through the eyes of a team of scientists and an underwater robot called Isis will be shown in selected cinemas across the UK next month. The documentary, How Deep Is Your Love, offers a playful, irreverent and bittersweet look at our anthropocentric view of Earth, as it switches perspective from humans to deep sea animals and back again. It follows a research team from the Natural History Museum (NHM) in London, who sail for 12 days to reach a remote region called the Clarion Clipperton Zone, a biodiversity-rich area of the Pacific between Hawaii and Mexico. It takes Isis five hours to make the 3-mile (5km) descent to the bottom of this harsh world, where sunlight cannot penetrate, and where nodules rich in minerals mark it out as a hotspot for industrial mining. Continue reading...

data.title: Doom Painting by AK Blakemore review – a dazzling epic of the Peasants’ Revolt
data.description: This recklessly ambitious doorstopper follows the 16 days of England’s medieval uprising from a vast array of viewpoints, and in startlingly rich prose AK Blakemore’s third novel tells the story of the Peasants’ Revolt of 1381, when commoners of all classes – not only peasants, but merchants, servants, smugglers, and some local lords and officials – rebelled at the imposition of a poll tax and rampaged through southern England, burning records of debts, killing their oppressors and laying waste to their homes. The book closely follows the events of the rebellion’s 16 days, employing a vast array of points of view, including the young king Richard II, several of his courtiers, dozens of elements of the rebellious Commons, a porpoise and a runaway horse. The title suggests the novel’s portrayal of these events as an inevitable reckoning; a “doom painting” was a picture of the Last Judgment on the wall of a medieval church. As a book of this scope must be, it’s a doorstopper. As any novel by Blakemore will be, it’s dazzlingly rich in lexical glamour, and this is likely to be any reader’s lasting impression of the book. Sometimes it feels as if the author is out to use every word in the English language in a startling, aestheticised, puckish way that expands both the word and the world. The result can be joyously silly. Who else would give us slugs that “blurb their elementary forms from out of the undergrowth to begin a dank and toothless festa ”, or “lunar-brilliantined mud”? But there is also gravity and passion here, especially when she intimately imagines the lives of the commoners: “they rise, to fry eggs in butter and pork fat; they rise, to whet knives on scarred stone; they rise, to braid the manes of their draught horses; they rise, to count arrows; they rise, setting aside their glitchy dreams of hairy stars and blue-skinned devils; they rise, fearful and powerful, into the bright day.” The cheekily anachronistic appearance of “glitchy” in this medieval scene is typical of Blakemore’s method. All forms of language, high and low, archaic and modern, are here. Her use of detail to convey a historical scene is also extraordinary: the barber’s chair where “a crowd has gathered beneath the ribboned pole to watch the draining of a cyst”; the brewer with “a grotty beard, chlorotic with hops, [that] hangs down almost to his belt”; or “the horseflies waltzing over the liquefying flesh of severed heads”. Continue reading...

data.title: Babystar review – a new arrival upends camera-ready life in disturbing family influencer satire
data.description: Every ethical issue surrounding parents vlogging their kids’ childhoods for money is raised in Joscha Bongard’s debut, but it releases the dysfunctional tension too easily When teenager Luca (Maja Bons) wants to watch the film of her birth, she finds it on YouTube. Same with the sweet, thoughtful chat her mum gave her about periods when she was nine or 10; it was filmed in the family’s podcast studio. None of life’s special moments go unmonetised in this satire from Germany, a horror story of family dysfunction. It’s a look at the dark side of the family influencer industry, raising just about every possible ethical question about parents vlogging their kids’ childhoods, and it’s impressively disturbing, up to a point. Sixteen-year-old Luca is the only child of Stella (Bea Brocks) and Chris (Liliom Lewald), social media stars who make viral videos of their perfect-looking family life for their 4 million followers. They live in a beautiful, sterile minimalist home in the countryside, and we often watch them through CCTV cameras fitted in every room. Shrewdly, first time film-maker Joscha Bongard doesn’t portray Stella and Chris as monsters; they love their daughter Luca, who they affectionately call Nunki. But fundamentally they do their best parenting in front of the camera, all bright smiles and proud affectionate glances. Continue reading...

data.title: Shadows of Beirut review – chaos and crisis as woman goes back to birth city in fractured Covid-era drama
data.description: A London-dwelling émigrée goes back to Lebanon to see her dying father in this somewhat overwrought film examining a difficult childhood This somewhat overwrought drama was apparently shot during the Covid-19 pandemic, partly in the city of the title and partly on sets in a Bulgarian studio. Its higgledy-piggledy production schedule perhaps accounts for the film’s fractured, frenetic quality and the feeling that the characters are perpetually in motion. Mind you, to be fair, the shredded editing might also be meant to reflect the distraught mental state of protagonist Lana (Tala Calil, also co-writer and producer) and the energy of the city itself, a municipality ravaged by wars that also has some of the most chaotic traffic in the Middle East. There’s even a scene where Lana’s new friend Sirine (Flavia Bechara) is driving and wants to take her coat off so she makes Lana take the wheel, much to Lana’s terror and distress, a nonchalance about safety believable for a city where traffic lights appear to be only a suggestion. That said, Lana has a lot going on so she’s easily rattled. She left Beirut 25 years earlier, and has only come back to see her biological father of whom she has only negative memories, from a childhood blighted by his alcoholism and violence. These days she lives in London with her boyfriend Ben (Michael E Rodgers) and her mother, but the former relationship is also rocky due to Lana’s OCD. She’s obsessed with wearing as much sanitary PPE kit as possible, including not just an N95 (in UK FFP2) mask but one of those full-face clear plastic ones, too. However, she suddenly finds the strength to stop wearing all the gear when she gets back to Beirut and reconnects with her cousin Rami (Assaad Bouab). She starts to open up a bit more, and befriends the aforementioned Sirine, who helps Lana when she’s having a panic attack at the hospital. By slow degrees she works up enough fortitude to face her father before he dies, but that means confronting some family secrets she never knew. Continue reading...

data.title: Heart of the action: why organ couriers are cinema’s new heroes
data.description: Whether its a nod to frontline Covid heroes or a return to biology in a world of digital noise, there’s a rich vein of new films featuring organ deliveries, including Runner and the latest Resident Evil Hollywood loves a ticking clock – especially when there’s a delivery involved. For decades, dangerous cargo has been entrusted to certain types of action hero: spies, soldiers, hitmen, Jason Statham. Lately, however, Hollywood seems interested in a different kind of hero – not to mention a different kind of cargo. Forget your nuclear launch codes, stolen diamonds and mysterious briefcases, for human organs are the new MacGuffins du jour, and the medical professionals charged with getting them to the ICU have become unlikely action heroes. When Post Script was first announced in June, several media reports assumed the nine-track album contained recordings that the final Fall lineup were working on before the singer’s death, in January 2018. However, it subsequently emerged that it contains unused studio vocals recorded between 2001 and 2014, to which longtime Fall associates Ed Blaney and Simon “Ding” Archer have posthumously added music. data.title: ‘Being in Madness kept some of them out of jail’: how the baggy-trousered nutty boys made a guerrilla cinema classic
data.description: From a jail-inspired light sabre fight to the moment a sax-player flew, Take It or Leave It brilliantly captured the hit-makers’ grimy origins. Will the film’s return see it finally honoured as a music movie landmark? It’s March 1981 and Madness are revisiting the haunts of their recent youth with a film crew in tow. In the 18 months since releasing their debut single, The Prince, the group have become the UK’s most beloved hit-makers, their ascent abetted by inventive music videos that have left viewers of Top of the Pops and Tiswas believing a man could fly – while blowing a sax. But this new project is something else. Instead of squandering their newfound wealth on fast cars and country piles, the seven-piece have invested in a semi-fictional big-screen telling of their origin story that tempers their trademark “nuttiness” with a kitchen-sink realism suiting their working-class roots. While Take It or Leave It sank into obscurity soon after release, a new 4K restoration has primed the film for rediscovery as a time-capsule of grimy 70s London, and perhaps cinema’s most honest depiction of the challenges involved in trying to get a band together. Continue reading...

data.title: Autumn by Kate Mosse review – tender reflections on time and place
data.description: The author of Labyrinth on the turning of the seasons and the lore and landscape of her beloved Sussex Kate Mosse’s new book is a love-song to West Sussex, part of a series designed to bring out its authors’ personal connections to a home landscape. It began last year, with Michael Morpurgo welcoming spring in Devon, where he has lived – at the farm that inspired War Horse – for over 50 years; and then Val McDermid celebrating winter in Scotland, where she grew up and still lives . Bernardine Evaristo will explore summer soon – but, meanwhile, we have Mosse, also deeply and endearingly rooted in her chosen patch. Mosse grew up in the village of Fishbourne. She now lives in Chichester, where she got to know her husband when they revised for A-levels in the shadow of the Bishop’s Palace, and held hands when she turned 17 on the day of the city’s annual Sloe Fair. Twenty-three years later, they celebrated her 40th there, with their children. Today, they live with his 90-something mother Granny Rosie – also “Sussex to her bones” – who remembers watching cattle herded in fields where a supermarket now stands. Continue reading...

data.title: Celebrity, sex and motherhood misery: the 10 best books by Rachel Cusk … ranked!
data.description: From an abstract portrait of an actor who might be Natalie Portman to a groundbreaking work of autofiction, we rate the best from the coolly controversial author In Cusk’s headline-grabbing latest, a writer invents the biography of a film star who sounds very like Natalie Portman. Set in the now standard late-Cusk sans serif typeface (no frivolous flourishes!), Life of M serves up observations on fame in a light fictional coating. “To always be playing a part is to have no home.” Having made her name as a devilishly good creator of brainy social comedies, Cusk’s pivot to wintry autofiction since the Outline trilogy appears to have reached its logical conclusion in this flat, abstracted portrait of empty celebrity. The New York Times called it “rarefied, cosmopolitan, self-serious”. Sample line: “Everything I did or said in her company was false. All he needs is big hair and leg warmers and listening to, I don’t know, synthetic pop, and he’d be right back in 1985.” Continue reading...

data.title: Control Resonant review – save New York from paranormal phenomena
data.description: PlayStation 5, Xbox, PC; Remedy A surprisingly conventional game from a famously weird developer, this sequel to 2019’s Control is accomplished but safe This is an arthouse action game from Finnish developer Remedy, masters of exactly this type of thing. It’s a sequel, however, so not only must it clear the high bar that its strikingly distinctive predecessor has set – it must also ideally arrive with a bushel of new ideas. There are clear and valuable strengths here in character progression and the lustrous presentation of its paranormal world, but Resonant doesn’t feel as enjoyably recondite or expansive in its influences as 2019’s Control did. As you wander New York brandishing supernatural abilities against glowing orange foes, the sad sense creeps in that you might be playing any number of games. As paranormal event survivor Jesse Faden, your journey through the original Control was like a sequence of playable Twilight Zone episodes, battling prosaic household objects with supernatural properties that teased and twisted reality inside an endlessly fascinating supernatural government bureau called the Oldest House. You’d navigate architecturally impossible spaces bridging the subconscious and the bricks-and-mortar world, in order to defeat a malevolent fridge. That’s broadly true again in Resonant, albeit with diminishing returns. This time you’re playing as Jesse’s brother Dylan, waking up after years of containment in the Oldest House to find its contents have escaped into downtown Manhattan. So you head out of the interesting place, and into a setting you’ve explored before in Marvel’s Spider-Man , The Division , Max Payne , and others ad infinitum. Continue reading...

data.title: Silent Hill: Townfall review – shame and suffering on the Scottish coast
data.description: PlayStation 5 (version played), PC; Screen Burn Tragedy, and an apocalyptic fog, befall a fishing community. It is up to outsider Simon to offer some kind of closure You spend a considerable portion of Silent Hill: Townfall in a kind of foetal position, cowering behind objects that will be eerily familiar to anyone who lived in the UK during the 1990s. Cars seem to be modelled on the era’s boxy Volkswagen Golfs; logos adorning phone boxes should narrowly escape the attention of copyright lawyers at BT Group. (For millennials, the deja vu will likely intensify the horror, as if stepping back into a childhood nightmare.) Simon, the nerdy, unassuming star of the game, pokes his head around corners to catch a glimpse of the demonic entities that wish to maim him, before shrinking back down again with a downwards motion of the analogue stick. In such moments, it’s easy to imagine him wrapping his arms around his knees, clasping his eyes shut and wishing himself away from this place. The game’s setting, St Amelia, is based on the fishing communities of the East Neuk of Fife. The terror lurking here is wonderfully specific: absent lairds, island poverty, an oil-drilling corporation. Anguished beasts lumber down quaint streets lined with sandstone houses and fluttering bunting. This venerable horror series may have shifted to Scotland, yet we remain firmly in classic Silent Hill territory – weather and all. St Amelia finds itself suffused in supernatural fog and the vast majority of its inhabitants have vanished following some kind of mass tragedy. The artful, evocative presentation is such that you can almost taste the in-game air, the briny seaside tang diluted by rainy mist. Continue reading...

Twenty-five years later, the Alexander McQueen brand returned from the Paris schedule to a creepily beautiful subterranean 17th century London chapel, with steel harnesses, bulky ankle strapped heels that looked like electronic monitoring tags, and a chain mail dress of tiny silver skulls. data.title: ‘Jaw-dropping’ El Niño bursts through temperature record months before peak
data.description: ‘Godzilla-level’ phenomenon is supercharging the climate crisis and will have a huge impact on communities across the world The “jaw-dropping” El Niño currently heating up the planet has burst through the highest temperature ever recorded for the phenomenon, several months before its expected peak. The latest data shows the temperature rise at the heart of El Niño in the Pacific Ocean has now reached 3.05C. That is higher than the 3.02C set in late November 2015, the previous high set in the 150 years of modern records. This temperature is measured against the average of 1991-2020. Continue reading...

data.title: Einstein’s ‘spooky action’ survives one of the most extreme tests yet: CERN finds heavy Z bosons can become quantum-entangled
data.description: Physicists at CERN's Large Hadron Collider have found strong evidence for quantum entanglement.  Two short-lived Z bosons, produced from a Higgs boson decay, showed quantum correlations.  This observation confirms quantum mechanics' strange predictions in extreme energy environments.  Researchers reconstructed Z boson properties from their decay products for analysis.  Future experiments will further investigate quantum phenomena at even higher energies.

data.title: Oregon introduced beachgrass to hold shifting sand in place; it later changed the entire dune system
data.description: In 1910, Oregon introduced European beachgrass to stabilise shifting dunes near Coos Bay. The plant succeeded but spread widely, covering much of the dune system and changing sand movement. As open, shifting habitats declined, native plants and animals adapted to moving dunes, including the endangered Western Snowy Plover, also lost important habitat.

data.title: 500 Iron Age iron bars found in Austria reveal a 1-tonne cargo transported 2,000 years ago
data.description: Archaeologists found over 500 forged iron bars in the Danube River.  This discovery represents Europe's largest known Iron Age iron assemblage.  Radiocarbon dating places these bars in the Late Iron Age, between 4th and 1st centuries BC.  The bars likely represent cargo lost during river transport along the Danube.  This significant find highlights the scale of Iron Age iron production and trade.

data.title: DN Debatt. ”Nu sätter vi stopp för chockräkningar hos veterinären”
data.description: DN DEBATT. I valrörelsen lovade alla partier djurägarna lägre kostnader, men inget av förslagen kommer att sänka priserna i närtid. Därför åtar vi oss att stärka pristransparensen och tydligheten – veterinärräkningen ska inte vara en överraskning. I gengäld begär vi politiska åtgärder som ger verklig effekt på prisbilden, skriver företrädare för djursjukvårdens företag.

data.title: Veelbelovend, die wijk Rijnenburg met z’n duizenden nieuwe woningen. Maar je moet wel met een tram komen waarvoor geen geld is
data.description: In 2024 tekenden ministeries, provincie, gemeenten en marktpartijen een akkoord voor een nieuwe grote woonwijk. data.title: Poslanci poprvé jednají podle nových pravidel. Řečníky omezila na půl hodiny
data.description: Už žádné mnohahodinové projevy, jako když Tomio Okamura v minulém volebním období blokoval jednání Sněmovny téměř jedenáct hodin. Poslanci poprvé jednají podle nových pravidel, která omezí dlouhé projevy. I řečníci s přednostním právem - šéfové stran a klubů i členové vlády mají nově na své vystoupení maximálně půl hodiny. A víc ani ťuk.

data.title: Tělo nalezené v jezeře Most patřilo pohřešovanému mladíkovi, potvrdila policie
data.description: Pitva potvrdila, že utonulý v jezeře Most je devatenáctiletý mladík, po kterém policie pátrala od letní bouřky v regionu. Případ policejní vyšetřovatel odloží, protože na úmrtí se nepodílel žádný jiný člověk a nebyl spáchán trestný čin. Tělo našel soukromý potápěč z Polska minulý týden ve čtvrtek.

data.title: Martin Kuba
data.description: Martin Kuba je od listopadu 2020 jihočeským hejtmanem. Občanští demokraté získali na jihu Čech po volbách v září 2024 většinu a v kraji vládnout dál a sami. Bývalý ministr průmyslu a obchodu ve vládě Petra Nečase i dočasný předseda ODS byl do listopadu 2024 i předsedou Asociace krajů ČR. V listopadu 2025 z ODS odešel a v březnu 2026 založil hnutí Naše Česko, jehož se stal předsedou.

data.title: Dívka na drogách pokousala personál nemocnice a předstírala zástavu srdce
data.description: K neobvykle divokému zásahu vyjížděli v úterý ráno strážníci v Pardubicích. Na úrazové ambulanci krotili agresivní osmnáctiletou pacientku na drogách, jež kolem sebe zběsile kousala. Běsnění navíc neustalo ani při následném transportu, kdy dívka cestou na záchytnou stanici opakovaně sehrála srdeční kolaps.

data.title: Náměstí není exponát, ale živý prostor, hodnotí lídr Pirátů Pavel Bosák

data.title: Hlasování o nedůvěře vládě bude do voleb. Do konce týdne oznámíme, řekl Grolich
data.description: Podpisy pro žádost o mimořádnou schůzi k hlasování o nedůvěře vládě Andreje Babiše již podle šéfa ODS Martina Kupky opozice má. „Ještě se poradíme, kdy ho přesně vyvoláme,“ řekl iDNES.cz Kupka. „Do voleb to rozhodně proběhne,“ uvedla šéfka klubu Pirátů Olga Richterová. „Oznámíme to do konce týdne,“ řekl iDNES.cz šéf lidovců Jan Grolich.

data.title: Reakce na bojkot médií. Bílý dům spustil Trump TV, vysílá jen prezidentovy úspěchy
data.description: Bílý dům oznámil spuštění Trump TV, která bude 24 hodin denně, sedm dní v týdnu vysílat zásadní projevy a nejpopulárnější momenty amerického prezidenta Donalda Trumpa. Krok přichází poté, co Trumpova administrativa vypověděla tři média z Bílého domu a ostatní stanice následně ze solidarity začaly bojkotovat jeho tiskovky. Kritici Trumpa mluví o autoritářském jednání.

Krok přichází poté, co Trumpova administrativa vypověděla tři média z Bílého domu a ostatní stanice následně ze solidarity začaly bojkotovat jeho tiskovky. Kritici Trumpa mluví o autoritářském jednání.

data.title: Překopnutý kabel ochromil dopravu v okolí New Yorku. Rušily se stovky letů
data.description: Výpadek komunikačních linek v klíčovém středisku řízení letového provozu ve Filadelfii v pondělí na několik hodin výrazně ochromil leteckou dopravu na severovýchodě Spojených států. Problémy zasáhly všechna hlavní letiště v oblasti New Yorku, nejvážnější situace byla na letišti Newark, kde se velká část provozu prakticky zastavila.

data.title: Co měsíc, to státní svátek. Jak na podzim vychází volno a jak mají otevřeno obchody
data.description: Co se volna týče, je rok 2026 nezvykle štědrý, což platí i o nadcházejícím podzimu. Všechny tři podzimní státní svátky připadají na pracovní dny. Jeden z nich zajistí prodloužený víkend automaticky, ty zbylé dva s trochou šikovnosti také. Záleží jen na tom, kolik dní dovolené budou pracující ochotni obětovat. A zaměstnavatelé ochotni povolit.

data.title: Motivace penězi. Vojtěch navrhuje odměnu za preventivní prohlídky a screening
data.description: Lidé by za splnění účasti na všech preventivních prohlídkách a screeningových vyšetřeních, které jsou pro jejich věk dostupné, mohli od zdravotní pojišťovny získat pět set až tisíc pět set korun. Řekl to vrchní ředitel sekce ekonomiky a zdravotního pojištění ministerstva zdravotnictví Jan Zapletal na dnešní tiskové konferenci k novele veřejného zdravotního pojištění, která bonus zavádí.

data.title: Vzhůru na Petřín! Nadšenci kvůli první jízdě lanovkou vstávali už ve tři ráno
data.description: Přivstali si, aby na vlastní kůži zažili její oficiální premiéru. Petřínská lanovka ve své obnovené premiéře svezla v úterý v 7 hodin ráno své první cestující. Někteří z nich postávali u stanice Újezd už o půl hodiny dříve. „Jedu sem až z Mostu, vstával jsem ve tři,“ sdělil redaktorce iDNES.cz při čekání jeden z přítomných nadšenců. Další partička se rozhodla s vozem závodit a chystala se svah na Petřín paralelně s jedoucím vozem vyběhnout.

data.title: Kdo vyřeší dopravu ve městě, vyhraje volby. V Hranicích se řeší i veřejný pořádek
data.description: Doprava je pro Hranice na Přerovsku jedno z klíčových témat. Již brzy se otevře klíčová spojnice, tzv. Palačovská spojka, která odvede z Hranic tranzitní kamionovou dopravu a obyvatelům města by se tak mělo ulevit. Jaká další dopravní odlehčení se chystají? I to byla jedna ze tří otázek iDNES.cz pro lídry devíti politických stran a uskupení, jež se v Hranicích ucházejí o vstup do zastupitelstva.

data.title: Tahač s třiceti tunami uhlí sjel ze silnice, hrozil únik plynu
data.description: Pondělní odpoledne v Moravskoslezském kraji poznamenaly dvě vážné dopravní nehody. U Oldřichovic na Třinecku narazil řidič osobního auta do stromu a s těžkými zraněními skončil v umělém spánku. V Havířově - Dolní Suché vyprošťovali hasiči havarovaný tahač vezoucí 30 tun uhlí, který ohrožoval plynovou přípojku.

data.title: Naftali Bennett
data.description: Pravicový a nacionalistický Naftali Bennett je veteránem izraelské politiky. Zprvu podnikatel a později milionář se během posledních dvaceti let na politické scéně propracoval řadou ministerských funkcí. Po úspěchu ve volbách roku 2021 také vystřídal dlouholetého premiéra Benjamina Netanjahua, po pádu vlastní vlády se však z politiky stáhl. Dnes se snaží o návrat na výsluní.

data.title: Němec si z Česka vezl prostitutku bez dokladů. Na hranici je oba čekal malér
data.description: Policie v Bavorsku zastavila Němce, který si k sobě domů vezl z českého nevěstince prostitutku. Protože žena původem z Nigérie neměla žádné platné cestovní doklady, bude se nyní muž zodpovídat z napomáhání k nelegálnímu překročení hranic, napsal zpravodajský portál TAG24.

data.title: Grupo de 22 países quer manter apertado e em mãos humanas o controlo da IA
data.description: A criação de um órgão de supervisão global e a necessidade de manter a Inteligência Artificial (IA) "sob direção, supervisão e controlo humanos" são duas das diretivas que constam de um documento publicado pelo site Politico esta segunda-feira e que foi para já subscrito por 22 países. data.description: Chefes de Estado e de Governo de 193 países reúnem-se na sede da ONU, em Nova Iorque, entre 22 e 28 de setembro, onde vão discutir os desafios globais que consideram prioritários. data.title: S&P keeps Botswana investment grade, but…

data.title: Cameroun : Sara TIMB rend hommage au député Samuel Moth
data.description: © ST Après une consécration à l’Ambassade des États-Unis au Cameroun à travers le Prix 35 Under 35 Cameroon Excellence Youths Awards, Sara TIMB, poétesse camerounaise multi récompensée, doctorante en biotechnologies végétales, entrepreneure sociale et digne fille Banen (Indikbiakat ) au rayonnement international, s'est offert un moment fort avec celui qu’elle appelle affectueusement « Papa » : l’honorable Samuel Moth, élite de la communauté Banen, dont le parcours, l’attachement à sa terre, l’engagement pour sa communauté et la générosité ont marqué son regard. Au-delà du festin d’honneur qu’il lui a réservé, du Mùtún, ce pagne traditionnel Banen dont il l’a personnellement revêtue. Et du soutien qu’il lui a spontanément apporté, c’est, en filigrane, le portrait d’un grand homme Banen qu’elle dessine : celui d’un bâtisseur dont les gestes, la générosité et l’exemplarité continuent de faire jaillir autour de lui des possibilités pour les autres. Si Sara TIMB, après un rayonnement international ponctué par un échange avec le président Emmanuel Macron et une sélection parmi les « 31 voix des féminismes africains » de la Fondation de l’Innovation pour la Démocratie dirigée par le Pr Achille Mbembe, a tenu à ce que le député Samuel Moth soit le premier à la recevoir, c’est qu’au-delà de l’affection mutuelle qu’ils se vouent, elle trouve dans son parcours une véritable niche de leçons pour la jeunesse. Jointe par la Rédaction de Journal du Cameroun, la poétesse explique : « Le parcours de mon père, l’Honorable Moth Samuel, est une belle et rare leçon d’excellence, d’engagement, de résilience, de solidarité, de modestie et de générosité. Il est ce beau trésor que le ciel a déposé sur les bords du Nkam, à Indikbiakat, confirmant une nouvelle fois que ce n’est pas seulement sur les rives du Wouri, du Moungo ou du Nyong que pouvaient naître des Hommes solidement attachés à la terre qui les porte, qui rougissent de ce qui est honteux, évincent la médiocrité et tiennent à distance ces tiers gêneurs et déraisonnables que sont le nombrilisme et l’individualisme, afin de s’employer inlassablement à la transformation durable et au rayonnement des leurs et de leur village. Ses actions sont salutaires. Les valeurs qu’il incarne se lisent elles aussi et rendent témoignage à la richesse de ses préoccupations, à la grandeur et à la noblesse de sa mission de vie. C’est forte de cette conviction, en tant que fille Banen, que j’ai tenu à ce qu’il soit le premier à me recevoir après mes belles prouesses à l’international. Il a inauguré au sein de notre communauté une conception neuve du service des siens. La bravoure et la constante assiduité avec lesquelles il veille à inscrire dignement son empreinte salutaire dans la défense des intérêts des Banen, notamment dans le dossier de la forêt d’Ebo, nonobstant le vacarme des médisances, en sont l’illustration saisissante. Cette soif d'œuvrer pour son village et pour les siens a souvent été pris d’assaut par de vilains esprits qui croient, à tort, pouvoir ensevelir ses actes sous le mucus gluant de faux narratifs et de billevesées. Mais que nenni ! l'Honorable Moth Samuel demeure debout comme un phare au milieu d'une mer démontée, balayant de ses faisceaux lumineux et les ténèbres traîtresses et l'écume des vagues en furie. Son appétit pour le service des siens est bien forte, irrépressible, ancré dans sa chair à tel point qu'elle ne puisse consentir à disparaitre. Son parcours m’apprend, comme à toute autre jeune, qu’on peut venir de loin, de si bas, et aller très loin, si haut, sans jamais se laisser rebuter par les mauvaises langues ni par les petites mains qui s’escriment à ne faire que du mal. Sa trajectoire académique, professionnelle et politique offre une démonstration topique de ce que sont l’excellence, l’ambition, la discipline et la résilience. C’est donc logiquement que je crois que, sans avoir jamais prétendu être un exemple, il est devenu exemplaire par ses actions, ses valeurs et son attachement à notre identité. » Concernant le moment d'exception qu'elle a partagé avec lui, Sara TIMB raconte une rencontre émouvante : « Ce mercredi 16 septembre 2026, je suis allée présenter mon trophée du 35 Under 35 Cameroon Youth Excellence Awards à mon père, l’Honorable Moth Samuel. Je pensais venir lui présenter un prix. Je ne savais pas que j’allais, moi aussi, recevoir quelque chose de beaucoup plus grand qu’un présent. Il m’avait préparé un festin. Un véritable festin, pensé avec cette générosité qu’on lui reconnaît et qui ne cherche pas simplement à offrir, mais à honorer. Parmi les choses qui donnent à son action sa force et sa portée, il y a cette capacité singulière à transformer les moments fédérateurs en véritables exercices de transmission, où les réussites des uns deviennent des possibles pour les autres. Sans que je ne m’en doute, il avait convié trois jeunes exceptionnels de notre communauté afin qu’ils soient témoins de ce moment. Son épouse, dans le même élan, avait invité ses deux nièces afin qu’elles puissent, elles aussi, s’inspirer de la petite femme que je suis. Et que dire de ce geste fort avec le _Mùtún_ ? De ses propres mains, il m’a revêtue du _Mùtún_ , tissu traditionnel de l’ethnie Banen, que je n’avais encore jamais porté de ma vie. Tissé à la main, précieux dans sa sobriété et chargé de notre mémoire collective, ce tissu, qu’il m’a fait porter en l’accompagnant de paroles fortes, n’est pas qu’un vêtement. Il est un symbole. Et la force de ce geste dépasse largement sa portée symbolique. Autant il m’honore profondément, autant il m’engage. Et je fais le pari optimiste d’être à la hauteur. Ce moment passé avec le couple Moth et mes frères de la communauté Banen est gravé dans ma mémoire. Je voudrais terminer par une note beaucoup plus personnelle : _Papa,_ Des tréfonds d’Iboti jusqu’à l’Assemblée Nationale du Cameroun, en passant par une vie professionnelle riche et combien remplie, il y a un chemin. Un chemin long, très long, parsemé d’embûches. Ce chemin-là, d’aucuns l’envient sans pouvoir en parcourir le dixième ; d’autres encore l’admirent à distance, reprochant à la nature de t’avoir tant gratifié et cultivant, dans le secret de leurs cœurs, des sentiments moins nobles. Mais d’autres, heureusement, le saluent avec déférence. Parce qu’au final, elles/ils sont nombreux.ses celles et ceux qui voudraient t’avoir pour frère ; pour ami ; ou encore pour mari. Mais moi, je t’ai comme père. Pour cette grâce dont je n’ai point fini de mesurer la portée, j'émets le vœu que tu puisses toujours demeurer ce jaillissement continu qu’à grand-peine on aveugle.» Cet article Cameroun : Sara TIMB rend hommage au député Samuel Moth est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

Au-delà du festin d’honneur qu’il lui a réservé, du Mùtún, ce pagne traditionnel Banen dont il l’a personnellement revêtue. Et du soutien qu’il lui a spontanément apporté, c’est, en filigrane, le portrait d’un grand homme Banen qu’elle dessine : celui d’un bâtisseur dont les gestes, la générosité et l’exemplarité continuent de faire jaillir autour de lui des possibilités pour les autres. Si Sara TIMB, après un rayonnement international ponctué par un échange avec le président Emmanuel Macron et une sélection parmi les « 31 voix des féminismes africains » de la Fondation de l’Innovation pour la Démocratie dirigée par le Pr Achille Mbembe, a tenu à ce que le député Samuel Moth soit le premier à la recevoir, c’est qu’au-delà de l’affection mutuelle qu’ils se vouent, elle trouve dans son parcours une véritable niche de leçons pour la jeunesse. Jointe par la Rédaction de Journal du Cameroun, la poétesse explique : « Le parcours de mon père, l’Honorable Moth Samuel, est une belle et rare leçon d’excellence, d’engagement, de résilience, de solidarité, de modestie et de générosité. Il est ce beau trésor que le ciel a déposé sur les bords du Nkam, à Indikbiakat, confirmant une nouvelle fois que ce n’est pas seulement sur les rives du Wouri, du Moungo ou du Nyong que pouvaient naître des Hommes solidement attachés à la terre qui les porte, qui rougissent de ce qui est honteux, évincent la médiocrité et tiennent à distance ces tiers gêneurs et déraisonnables que sont le nombrilisme et l’individualisme, afin de s’employer inlassablement à la transformation durable et au rayonnement des leurs et de leur village. Ses actions sont salutaires. Les valeurs qu’il incarne se lisent elles aussi et rendent témoignage à la richesse de ses préoccupations, à la grandeur et à la noblesse de sa mission de vie. C’est forte de cette conviction, en tant que fille Banen, que j’ai tenu à ce qu’il soit le premier à me recevoir après mes belles prouesses à l’international. Il a inauguré au sein de notre communauté une conception neuve du service des siens. La bravoure et la constante assiduité avec lesquelles il veille à inscrire dignement son empreinte salutaire dans la défense des intérêts des Banen, notamment dans le dossier de la forêt d’Ebo, nonobstant le vacarme des médisances, en sont l’illustration saisissante. Cette soif d'œuvrer pour son village et pour les siens a souvent été pris d’assaut par de vilains esprits qui croient, à tort, pouvoir ensevelir ses actes sous le mucus gluant de faux narratifs et de billevesées. Mais que nenni ! l'Honorable Moth Samuel demeure debout comme un phare au milieu d'une mer démontée, balayant de ses faisceaux lumineux et les ténèbres traîtresses et l'écume des vagues en furie. Son appétit pour le service des siens est bien forte, irrépressible, ancré dans sa chair à tel point qu'elle ne puisse consentir à disparaitre. Son parcours m’apprend, comme à toute autre jeune, qu’on peut venir de loin, de si bas, et aller très loin, si haut, sans jamais se laisser rebuter par les mauvaises langues ni par les petites mains qui s’escriment à ne faire que du mal. Sa trajectoire académique, professionnelle et politique offre une démonstration topique de ce que sont l’excellence, l’ambition, la discipline et la résilience. C’est donc logiquement que je crois que, sans avoir jamais prétendu être un exemple, il est devenu exemplaire par ses actions, ses valeurs et son attachement à notre identité. » Concernant le moment d'exception qu'elle a partagé avec lui, Sara TIMB raconte une rencontre émouvante : « Ce mercredi 16 septembre 2026, je suis allée présenter mon trophée du 35 Under 35 Cameroon Youth Excellence Awards à mon père, l’Honorable Moth Samuel. Je pensais venir lui présenter un prix. Je ne savais pas que j’allais, moi aussi, recevoir quelque chose de beaucoup plus grand qu’un présent. Il m’avait préparé un festin. Un véritable festin, pensé avec cette générosité qu’on lui reconnaît et qui ne cherche pas simplement à offrir, mais à honorer. Parmi les choses qui donnent à son action sa force et sa portée, il y a cette capacité singulière à transformer les moments fédérateurs en véritables exercices de transmission, où les réussites des uns deviennent des possibles pour les autres. Sans que je ne m’en doute, il avait convié trois jeunes exceptionnels de notre communauté afin qu’ils soient témoins de ce moment. Son épouse, dans le même élan, avait invité ses deux nièces afin qu’elles puissent, elles aussi, s’inspirer de la petite femme que je suis. Et que dire de ce geste fort avec le _Mùtún_ ? De ses propres mains, il m’a revêtue du _Mùtún_ , tissu traditionnel de l’ethnie Banen, que je n’avais encore jamais porté de ma vie. Tissé à la main, précieux dans sa sobriété et chargé de notre mémoire collective, ce tissu, qu’il m’a fait porter en l’accompagnant de paroles fortes, n’est pas qu’un vêtement. Il est un symbole. Et la force de ce geste dépasse largement sa portée symbolique. Autant il m’honore profondément, autant il m’engage. Et je fais le pari optimiste d’être à la hauteur. Ce moment passé avec le couple Moth et mes frères de la communauté Banen est gravé dans ma mémoire. Je voudrais terminer par une note beaucoup plus personnelle : _Papa,_ Des tréfonds d’Iboti jusqu’à l’Assemblée Nationale du Cameroun, en passant par une vie professionnelle riche et combien remplie, il y a un chemin. Un chemin long, très long, parsemé d’embûches. Ce chemin-là, d’aucuns l’envient sans pouvoir en parcourir le dixième ; d’autres encore l’admirent à distance, reprochant à la nature de t’avoir tant gratifié et cultivant, dans le secret de leurs cœurs, des sentiments moins nobles. Mais d’autres, heureusement, le saluent avec déférence. Parce qu’au final, elles/ils sont nombreux.ses celles et ceux qui voudraient t’avoir pour frère ; pour ami ; ou encore pour mari. Mais moi, je t’ai comme père. Pour cette grâce dont je n’ai point fini de mesurer la portée, j'émets le vœu que tu puisses toujours demeurer ce jaillissement continu qu’à grand-peine on aveugle.» Cet article Cameroun : Sara TIMB rend hommage au député Samuel Moth est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Les Américano-Camerounais Joel Hans Embiid et les Philadelphia 76ers peuvent-ils aller plus loin en playoffs NBA cette saison ?
data.description: © Yellowbet Les Philadelphia 76ers ont atteint les demi-finales de la Conférence Est la saison dernière après avoir terminé avec un bilan de 45 victoires pour 37 défaites. Leur parcours en playoffs s’est toutefois arrêté face aux New York Knicks, qui se sont imposés 4-0. Ce résultat donne à Philadelphia un objectif clair pour cette nouvelle saison : atteindre les finales de conférence. L’effectif possède suffisamment de talent pour y parvenir, même si beaucoup dépendra de la disponibilité de Joel Embiid. Les 76ers ont remporté leur série du premier tour contre Boston 4-3 après avoir été menés 3–1. Ils ont ensuite affronté une équipe des Knicks qui a mis en évidence les faiblesses de Philadelphia. Cette élimination sans concéder le moindre match a également soulevé des questions sur la capacité des 76ers à compter sur Embiid tout au long d'une longue campagne de playoffs. Embiid élève le plafond de Philadelphia Lorsqu’il est en bonne santé, Embiid offre à Philadelphia un scoreur d’élite et un défenseur intérieur de premier plan. Le septuple All-Star a affiché des moyennes de 26,9 points, 7,7 rebonds et 3,9 passes décisives en 38 matchs de saison régulière la saison dernière. Ses absences ont constitué un problème majeur. Embiid a manqué une grande partie de la saison et a fait son retour pendant la série contre Boston après avoir subi une appendicectomie. Il a ensuite été gêné par une entorse à la cheville et des douleurs à la hanche durant la série face aux Knicks. Philadelphia a besoin d’un Embiid en meilleure santé cette saison. Sa présence modifie la manière dont les adversaires défendent les 76ers et donne à l’équipe une option fiable dans le jeu placé. Le fait de pouvoir compter sur lui pendant les playoffs pourrait avoir un impact plus important sur les ambitions de Philadelphia que n’importe quel changement individuel dans l’effectif. Maxey et le reste de l’effectif Tyrese Maxey apporte aux 76ers un autre scoreur et créateur de haut niveau. Sa progression continue devrait réduire la pression exercée sur Embiid, qui ne devrait pas avoir à créer presque toutes les possessions importantes. Le reste de l’effectif aura également son importance. Philadelphia devra pouvoir compter sur une adresse régulière à trois points, sur des minutes solides de la part du banc et sur suffisamment de profondeur défensive pour tenir le rythme d’une série en sept matchs. La série contre les Knicks a montré ce qui peut se produire lorsque ces éléments ne fonctionnent pas ensemble. Philadelphia a eu du mal à suivre, avant de finalement perdre le quatrième match de 30 points. Pour aller plus loin en playoffs, Maxey et les joueurs qui entourent Embiid devront être réguliers lorsque les défenses concentreront leur attention sur le pivot. Les 76ers ne peuvent pas se permettre de longues séquences durant lesquelles leur attaque devient trop prévisible. Philadelphia peut-elle atteindre les finales de conférence ? Les 76ers ont déjà montré qu’ils étaient capables de remporter une série de playoffs difficile. Leur victoire 4-3 contre Boston la saison dernière les a obligés à revenir d’un déficit de 3-1, leur offrant une expérience précieuse avant une nouvelle campagne de postseason. Pour les fans qui suivent les matchs en livestream ou utilisent des betting apps in Cameroon , les perspectives de Philadelphia dépendront probablement en grande partie de l’état de santé d’Embiid. Sa disponibilité pourrait influencer les attentes autour de l’équipe plus que presque tout autre facteur. Une qualification pour les finales de conférence est envisageable si Embiid reste en bonne santé, si Maxey continue de progresser et si le reste de l’effectif répond présent pendant les playoffs. La saison dernière s’est terminée en demi-finales ; la prochaine étape consiste à trouver suffisamment de régularité pour franchir ce tour. Cet article Les Américano-Camerounais Joel Hans Embiid et les Philadelphia 76ers peuvent-ils aller plus loin en playoffs NBA cette saison ? est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: CITS26 : le Cameroun veut accélérer son ambition de hub numérique en Afrique centrale
data.description: © DR Réunis lors d’une conférence de presse le 18 septembre 2026, les organisateurs de la Cameroon innovation and Tech Summit (CITS) ont de nouveau évoqué leur volonté de faire du Cameroun un pôle majeur des services digitaux en Afrique centrale. En prélude à la deuxième édition du Cameroon innovation and Tech Summit (CITS), CITS26, qui se tiendra du 15 au 17 octobre 2026 au Palais des Congrès de Yaoundé, les acteurs clés de l’écosystème numérique camerounais ont échangé avec les professionnels des médias pour expliquer les enjeux technologiques et économiques du pays. La question centrale sera : ‘’ Comment le Cameroun peut-il tirer parti de la technologie, de l’entrepreneuriat et de son capital humain pour accélérer le développement durable ? L’évènement de trois jours réunira plus de 10.000 participants en présentiel et en ligne. En ligne de mire, innovateurs, entrepreneurs, jeunes talents, investisseurs, décideurs politiques et partenaires internationaux. Au cours de l’échange avec les journalistes, le directeur général de la CITS, Ayuk Etat a fait savoir qu’il s’agit d’une plateforme destinée à transformer les talents, l’innovation et l’ambition du Cameroun en opportunités durables. Il a rappelé l’urgence d’absorber le volume massif de diplômés arrivant sur le marché du travail. « Sur 120.000 jeunes diplômés des universités chaque année au Cameroun, le marché local ne propose que 6000 emplois formels, laissant environ 114 000 jeunes sans emplois » regrette le promoteur du CITS. Pour absorber le mal, le dirigeant préconise l’externalisation des services numériques à l’instar du modèle indien. Ayuk Etat évoque les atouts stratégiques énormes pour se positionner comme un géant du numérique dans la sous-région. Il cite entre autres, le bassin de talents bilingue que regorge le pays et un fuseau horaire aligné sur celui de l’Europe. Toutefois, relève le promoteur, la concrétisation de cette ambition est conditionnée par le renforcement des infrastructures de base notamment la fourniture de l’énergie électrique et l’accès à un internet de haut débit. « Avant de déployer l’I.A, le pays doit d’abord résoudre la question énergétique et mener à bien la digitalisation, le nettoyage et la sécurisation des données administratives, encore largement sur format papier.» Ayuk Etat pense que, sans ces prérequis, le pays continuera de consommer les modèles étrangers inadaptés aux besoins locaux. Présent sur le panel, le président de Cameroon digital tank, Lionel Mbiandjeu a relevé qu’il est important qu’aujourd’hui les acteurs de la Tech au Cameroun dans un endroit se retrouvent, montrent leurs compétences, leurs solutions, se questionnent sur les problématiques, essayent de les adresser en synergie pour qu’à la fin : « le potentiel que nous avons du Cameroun d’être un leader de la transformation digitale en Afrique puisse être une réalité. » Les intervenants ont également souligné que l’importance du CITS26 est de faire connaître et adopter les solutions développées au pays par des talents locaux, afin de créer des success-stories capables de rivaliser avec les géants régionaux. Cet article CITS26 : le Cameroun veut accélérer son ambition de hub numérique en Afrique centrale est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : une croissance à 3,2% en 2025 freinée par les troubles postélectoraux et la dette
data.description: © DR Selon le Baromètre économique de la CEMAC, le PIB réel du Cameroun n'a progressé que de 3,2% en 2025, le déficit courant s'est creusé à 4,2% du PIB contre 3,4% en 2024 et le déficit budgétaire à 2,2% contre 1,5%. L'inflation est retombée à 3,4% en décembre 2025, permettant à la BEAC de baisser son taux directeur de 4,75% à 4,5% en juin 2026, tandis que la dette publique recule légèrement à 43,8% du PIB. L'économie camerounaise avance au ralenti. En 2025, le PIB réel n'a augmenté que de 3,2%, tiré par la consommation privée et l'investissement, révèle le Baromètre économique de la CEMAC. Une performance en deçà du potentiel, plombée par les troubles postélectoraux et les mesures de confinement qui ont fortement freiné l'activité, en particulier dans les services. Sur le front extérieur, le tableau est contrasté. Malgré une bonne performance des exportations de fèves de cacao qui profite aux ménages ruraux, les baisses continues de la production d'huile et des exportations de grumes, conjuguées à une hausse des importations, ont creusé le déficit du compte courant de 3,4% du PIB en 2024 à 4,2% en 2025. La note positive vient de l'inflation, tombée à 3,4% en décembre 2025 grâce à une politique monétaire stricte, un contrôle des prix et une inflation importée moindre. Cette décrue a permis à la Banque des États de l'Afrique Centrale (BEAC) de reprendre en juin 2026 un assouplissement progressif, en réduisant son taux directeur de 4,75% à 4,5%, renversant ainsi le resserrement introduit fin 2025 pour préserver les avoirs extérieurs nets. Côté finances publiques, la pression s'accentue. Le déficit budgétaire est passé de 1,5% du PIB en 2024 à 2,2% en 2025, en raison de la baisse des recettes pétrolières et non pétrolières liée aux troubles. Le déficit primaire non pétrolier s'est creusé à 2,6%. Les dépenses courantes sont restées élevées du fait des élections, tandis que les dépenses en capital ont reculé. Le ratio de la dette publique sur le PIB a légèrement diminué à 43,8% fin 2025 contre 44,8% un an plus tôt. Une dette jugée soutenable, mais les risques de liquidité restent élevés : les recettes d'exportation ne couvrent pas entièrement le service de la dette extérieure et les paiements d'intérêts ont atteint 1,4% du PIB. Le budget 2026 tente de corriger le tir en priorisant la croissance inclusive, avec 50 milliards FCFA affectés à un fonds pour l'autonomisation des femmes et l'emploi des jeunes. Reste que la hausse du service de la dette réduit la marge de manœuvre pour les dépenses sociales. Cet article Cameroun : une croissance à 3,2% en 2025 freinée par les troubles postélectoraux et la dette est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
